summary: A 1941 Forest Service plan cab on BLM land near Shoshone, Idaho; lookout use ended in the 2000s and the cab is now an enclosed radio building.

facts.design: 14-by-14-foot ground cab, USFS Region 1 plan design
facts.status_note: No longer a lookout; converted to an enclosed radio building in the 2000s

staffing.status: no longer staffed as a lookout

access.note: Reached by an unsigned gravel road off U.S. 93. The cab is an enclosed radio building; no source describes visitor entry.

visit.trail_note: Unsigned gravel road off US-93 reaches the summit; a short hike or bike ride from the highway is also possible. The cab is an enclosed radio building.

facts.agency: Bureau of Land Management (Twin Falls District)

events.note: Register and firelookout.com both date the cab to 1941
Idaho Lookouts lists a cabin on the butte in the 1930s; the register does not mention one
Julius Imgard identified as the lookout in a Times-News report reprinted August 24, 1944
July 1945 fire of about 2,000 acres forced one man to leave the grazier's station and lookout tower
Last name on the personnel list: Paul Roberts, 1983-1985
Used for emergencies into the 2000s, then converted to a communications building. The register says into the 2000s; the climbing guide says early 2000s. Year is approximate.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Lookouts lists a cabin in the 1930s and a 1941 frame cabin. The register and firelookout.com date the current cab to 1941 and mention no earlier cabin. The story keeps 1941 and flags the 1930s cabin as uncorroborated.
Firelookout.com says the cab is an enclosed radio building; the climbing guide says radio tower. The same building is described in both, so the story says radio building.
A 2024 trip report says about 4 miles south of Shoshone; firelookout.com says 2 miles. The story gives the trip report figure and attributes the other.
The register gives 4,343 ft (1,324 m); firelookout.com gives 4337 ft. The difference is small and the register figure is used in the brief.

sources.title: Trip report on Notch Butte Lookout

notes_for_editor: Built year (1941), BLM ownership, the 2020 registration and the conversion to a radio building agree across sources. The 1944 and 1945 newspaper details come from Times-News reports reprinted on idaholookouts.weebly.com; the original newspapers were not checked. No source gives current access rules, so access is recorded as restricted, not confirmed. The 1930s cabin appears only on the Idaho Lookouts page. Staffing after the mid-1980s is not documented here. The distance from Shoshone conflicts: the trip report says about four miles, firelookout.com says two; the story attributes each.
